scope: offline static analysis and control-backed bounded tests only; no device access, no network requests, no blind key enumeration

experiment_1_twin_aes_differential_diges.description: Tests whether GH5 and S1 loader1 (or S5 V2.8 and V2.9 loader1) decrypt to any matching 16B plaintext blocks under the 5 verified legacy AES-128 keys across CBC (interior IV-independent + block 0 IV candidates), CFB128 (interior IV-independent + block 0), CFB8 (interior IV-independent), OFB (tail[:16]), and 5 CTR counter layouts (tail[:16]). Does not assume candidate_digest == SHA256(plaintext).

experiment_2_mt19937_twin_xor_linearity.description: Key/seed-independent and digest-independent test exploiting GF(2)-linearity of MT19937 twist and temper: if two ciphertexts encrypt the same 4096B plaintext via XOR with any two MT19937 streams at the same phase, their XOR C_A ^ C_B = S_A ^ S_B must satisfy the MT19937 recurrence.

experiment_3_tz10_parity_feedback_mt_wit.description: Tests three LE four-u32 seed rules: tail[:16] directly, tail[:16] XOR the TZ10 resident seed, and the fixed resident seed. Two pairs produce six pair tests/twelve candidate hashes. Only same-index 4B/16B comparisons are recorded; no BE-seed or cross-index tests were executed.

coverage.mt_model_boundary: Common plaintext, same word alignment/phase and standard no-feedback recurrence; other transformations untested

conclusions.claim: GH5 V2.8 (MC561, SHA-256 1c7e7538...) index 0 loader1 at file offset 0x1200..0x2200 (rel 0x1000 + 0x200) and S1 V2.4 (MC892, SHA-256 1c54dd84...) index 0 loader1 at file offset 0x1600..0x2600 (rel 0x1400 + 0x200) have identical size (4096B), destination (0x0), flags (3), and 32B candidate_digest (4913f493636ed435d185ca3e5bea7a49eec28195606c99845d38ec68d91ccc5b), while their 4096B raw payloads (6a654e0f... vs 84904a20...) and 16B tail prefixes (8d5ac04a... vs bd515433...) differ.

The +0x200 payload base offset is verified in-file by all flags==2 entries (4/4 in GH5 V2.8 and 7/7 in S1 V2.4 match SHA-256 with +0x200, 2/9 non-empty match without +0x200 (1/3 GH5 and 1/6 S1, coincidental filler matches)). The external reference S1___V24.bin.parts.json recorded unshifted relative offsets (off=5120=0x1400), which overlap the last 504B of the 53-entry directory table [0x1400, 0x15f8) and 8B zero padding [0x15f8, 0x1600).

Across the entire 4096B loader1 pair (GH5 vs S1), same-offset byte equality is 20/4096 (0.4883%), bit difference is 16490/32768 (50.3235%), and there are 0 matching 16B blocks at the same index (256), across any aligned indices (256x256=65,536), or across any unaligned 16B sliding windows (4081x4081=16,654,561). The same-model S5 V2.8 vs V2.9 index 0 loader1 pair (4096B, digest e009d688..., identical offset 0x1600 and model MC801, differing only in tail[:16]) exhibits the same full-payload divergence (14/4096 bytes equal, 50.6775% bits changed, 0/16,654,561 16B windows equal), ruling out file-offset or model-string alone as the sole cause of ciphertext divergence without per-entry tail[:16] or per-build randomization.

Under the five actual legacy keys (G3 V1.2, GF2 V1.1, GF3 V1.2, GH2 V1.1 and GX1 V1.1), the implemented nine AES mode/counter layouts yield zero same-index blocks; CBC/CFB128/OFB/CTR also yield zero cross-index blocks, while CFB8 has no cross-index statistic. This bounds a common-plaintext model under the listed parameters, not all AES or KDF possibilities. The MT19937 result assumes common plaintext and common word alignment/phase. TZ10 parity tests use three LE seed rules on two pairs (six pair tests/twelve hashes), with no BE-seed or cross-index coverage.

Across modern UPD firmwares, loader1 divides into two structural generations: 4096B at index 0 (dest 0x0, followed by loader2 at dest 0x1000 in GH5/S1/S5 and dest 0x20000 in GH4) vs 131072B at index 1 after a 0-byte boot entry (dest 0x0 in S5M2/S1M2/SL3). GH5 V2.8, S1 V2.4, and external reference S1H V2.8 metadata share the exact 4096B loader1 candidate digest 4913f493..., making this 4KiB component the smallest cross-model shared-digest code-slot candidate.

Whether GH5 and S1 index 0 loader1 decrypt to the exact same 4096B plaintext, whether they share a key or key-derivation hierarchy, and the exact consumer formula for candidate_digest and tail[:16] remain unproven until a readable revision=0x200 / selector=3 consumer is located.

Whether candidate_digest (4913f493...) is computed over raw 4096B plaintext, unpadded payload, or a header+payload structure.
Whether tail[:16] is a direct cipher IV/nonce, a KDF salt/seed, or a wrapped per-entry key/tag.
Full S1H__V28.bin binary and a second version of GH5 or S1 are not in the local workspace.

next_steps.experiment: Locate the revision=0x200 / selector=3 consumer via the 92B directory stride (0x5c at base+0x2ec) and the unique loader1/loader2 boundary signature (dest=0x0, size=0x1000, followed by dest=0x1000), then trace how entry+0x1c (32B candidate_digest) and entry+0x3c (16B tail[:16]) are passed to the cipher/hash routines.

After a candidate key/KDF or consumer transform has actual readable-code or verified dump evidence, test both 4KiB loader1 pairs with full output hashes and format/consumer checks. Equality to the candidate digest is a conditional check until its plaintext coverage is established; metadata alone does not prove identical plaintext or a shared key.
